plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Wild poinsettias are tall, leggy shrubs. Their fiery red bracts, which are modified leaves, surround tiny yellow flower clusters. They light up tropical hillsides in the dry season. The same plant is a holiday favorite around the world.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (roughly November to February) in its native range
plants.location: Southern Mexico and Central America, in the tropical dry forests of Pacific-facing slopes
plants.funFact: The showy red parts are bracts, not petals. The real flowers are the small yellow-green cups at the center. The plant needs long nights to trigger its color change, which is why it blooms in December.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub opens rose-like blooms in cool weather. The flowers are silky and layered, with a boss of golden stamens. They brighten gardens when little else is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with many cultivars at peak in December in mild climates
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and coastal China. Widely grown in the southeastern United States, such as Georgia and the Carolinas, and in the UK and Europe.
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Japanese camellia seeds are pressed to make tsubaki oil, which is used in hair care and for polishing tools.

plants.name: Metrosideros excelsa
plants.description: A rugged coastal evergreen that clings to sea cliffs. In midsummer it erupts in crimson pom-pom flowers made of bright stamens. The blossoms turn the shoreline red.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere early summer, roughly late November through December, peaking around mid to late December
plants.location: Coastal North Island of New Zealand, including the Coromandel Peninsula and Northland
plants.funFact: Pōhutukawa blooms around Christmas, so it is known as New Zealand's Christmas tree. It can grow aerial roots down rocky cliffs and live for hundreds of years.
